utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. Would you please read aloud the affirmation that is shown to you on the card.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Good morning. Could you state your name for the record, please.

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Lizane Malaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And, Ms. Malaj, you were born on the 16th of April, 1963, in Guska, Djakovica municipality, were you?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And you're a Kosovo Albanian of Catholic faith.

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And in 1982, at the age of 19 you married Vat Malaj.

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And you moved to Korenica then, where your husband worked as a farmer.

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could we please have 65 ter Exhibit 615.02 pulled up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And while that is happening, Ms. Malaj, how many families were living in Korenica?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: As far as I know there were 70 houses at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And roughly how many persons were living in Korenica?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: But it's not a huge town; it's rather a village, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Yes, it is a village.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm waiting for the exhibit to pop up. We just would need one screen here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you mark, with the assistance of the usher, where your village, Korenica, is located, please, by drawing an arrow towards your village.

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Yes. The village of Korenice is here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you draw an arrow, please.

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: I don't think it came out as I expected.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The witness has, for the record, underlined one of the names in which Korenica was written on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you mark where your family courtyard was in Korenica, please, your family house, by encircling the location.

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you mark a little bit wider circle because --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can we maybe remove, because I think it's not very legible, can we maybe start afresh by just removing the markings made.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And if you now could mark a little bit broader circle at the location where you believe your family compound or your family courtyard is.

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. And can you mark a 1 next to this, please, the number 1.

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that your brother Nikoll Kabashi was also living with his family in another house in this family courtyard?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And by March 1999, how many children did you have?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: I had five children.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What's the name of your oldest child?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Blerim Malaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to take you now to the tensions in 1998. Can you tell us, when did you see for the first time Serbian forces in your area?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: In the spring, in May.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: In which year?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And what did you see?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: We saw tanks, AP Cs, Pinzgauers.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you mark on this map where you saw these tanks, APCs, and Pinzgauers, please.

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: On the road from Gjakove to Junik.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you mark the location, please.

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: For the record, the witness has marked four lines next to a grey road.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And can you mark a 2 next to these four lines, please.

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What else did you observe in the spring of 1998, near your house?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Near my house I saw some infantry soldiers or forces, paramilitaries, police.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you mark for us the location of these forces, please, by drawing a circle and a 3 next to this.

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Yes. Somewhere here, then. This is the house and ...

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Since both circles are so close to each other, for the record, the witness has marked above the circle which was mentioned with number 1 another circle and added the number 3 to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And in the summer of 1998, where did you stay overnight?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: We usually went to Guska, which is the neighbouring village. The men left home and went to the mountains above our houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Why did you leave and the men leave the family houses in the summer of 1998 at night?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: For protection reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Protection against what?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Protection from the Serbian forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What were the Serbian forces doing?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: At that time almost nothing happened in our village, but we left because we could see forces there that were on the main road, and they were shooting from different positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Shooting at what?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: They were shooting at Ramoc, Nec, and other villages that were close to ours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you mark Ramoc and Nec. Please encircle Ramoc first.

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And mark a 4 next to it.

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And now Nec, please, and mark a 5 next to it.

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to move on to the events in 1999 now, to be precise on Easter Monday. What information did you learn at the end of March 1999?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: On the Easter Monday, it was the 4th of April Milutin Prascevic came --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I just stop you here. Because I will come to the 4th of April in a second. I was asking you about the end of March, a few days before that, 4th of April. Do you remember what happened at the end of March 1999?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Yes. At that time Dragan Micunovic ordered a 15-year-old boy named Gjon Prelaj to separate men from the women, to tell them to leave for the mountains, and they wanted to move us to different locations by buses and other vehicles. But on the same day the men were again ordered to return to their homes. My son Blerim Malaj went with him. He was forced to go with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you just explain who was ordered? You said "us." Who was ordered by Dragan Micunovic?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: The villages of Korenice, all the men. Those who were in the village, he ordered them to leave the village, the men, and the women were ordered to remain there in their houses and later to be directed to different locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And who was Dragan Micunovic?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: He was the only one in our village. We had good relations with him, all of the villagers, until he gave us the order to leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you explain, you said he was the only one in our village. What ethnicity did Dragan Micunovic have?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: He was a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And what ethnicity did the other villagers in Korenica have?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: They were Albanians.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And what was the position of Dragan Micunovic in March 1999?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: He was in the Yugoslav Army. He was an officer, but I don't know his exact position.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. And what happened on Easter Monday, the 4th of April, 1999?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: On that day Milutin Prascevic, with other police colleagues, came to the transformer in Korenice, near Engjull Berisha's house and went to the house of the Dedaj family, and there they ordered the people to leave within three hours. This is what we did. We followed their order.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you, first of all, tell us who is Milutin Prascevic?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: He was a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I note the transcript has two spellings for his family name. Can you clarify -- or can you spell his last name.

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Milutin Prascevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. And what was his job?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: I don't know. I simply know that he was a policeman, but I don't know his function.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Why do you think he was a policeman?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: He was a policeman. He was to my house -- he came to my house with another policeman wearing a uniform, armed, and ordered us to leave the house and leave the cars behind, only take the tractors with us. And we followed his orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you tell me, what was Mr. Prascevic wearing when he came to your house? What clothes?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Blue.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And were these civilian clothes or ...

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: No, no. It was a uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And did you notice anything else on what Mr. Prascevic or his colleagues were wearing?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: The weapons. He was armed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And what arms did the gentleman wear?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Automatic rifles, everything that they wear as personal weapons. I don't know all their names. I know that this one, the automatic rifle or the machine-gun, he was wearing it on his arm and the pistol was on his side.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Did the gentleman tell you why you were ordered to leave that day?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: He told us to leave the place because we were Albanians. For what other reason?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And where did he tell you to go?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: To Albania.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And you mentioned before that the gentleman also went to other houses inside Korenica. What was the reaction of the villagers in Korenica to these suggestions or orders?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: They started leaving their houses immediately. A convoy was immediately formed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And how many persons were in that convoy?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: The entire village, I don't know the exact number.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. You mentioned before vehicles which you possessed. What vehicles did you take with you that day?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: We didn't dare take the cars with us. We just took the tractor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So at what point in time of the 4th of April, 1999, did the convoy leave Korenica?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: On the same day at Suhadoll, a kilometre further, Aca Micunovic came there with a colleague. I don't know who the colleague was, but I could recognise Aca. He ordered us to go back to the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you just before answer my previous question. At what point in time did you leave Korenica?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Sometime in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. And then you went to Suhadoll.

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you, looking at the map, indicate by encircling the location where Suhadoll is.

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Suhadoll is here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You have drawn a circle on the grey street. Can you mark a number 6 next to Suhadoll.

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And who was Aca Micunovic?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: He was Dragan's brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what Aca Micunovic's job was?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: At that time he was a local policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And where did he work?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: He was a village policeman. I don't know where he worked.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And what happened following his announcements or his -- the conversation?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: We returned to our houses and nothing happened to us until the 27th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. What I want to know from you is when you had left on the 4th of April in the afternoon Korenica, did you and your family leave voluntarily?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: No. We were forced to.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Who forced you?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Milutin Prascevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Did you know at the time in early 1999 that the NATO bombings had already started in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Had any of the NATO bombing affected your village, Korenica, by the 4th of April, 1999?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Was it because of NATO that you left the village on the afternoon of the 4th of April?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to move on to the 27th of April, 1999. What happened that day?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: It was a horrible, horrible day. It was a Tuesday. At 5.00 in the morning, the Serbian forces surrounded the village, the whole village, early in the morning. At 7.30 they came to my courtyard.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you just explain which village you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Korenice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And who came at 7.30 to your courtyard?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: The Serb forces, soldiers, paramilitaries, policemen, all of them. They had ribbons on their arms.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What colour were the ribbons?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Red.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And roughly how many men were coming to your courtyard?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Thirty-five. There were 35 around my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. And roughly how many men were wearing these red ribbons?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: I don't know the number, but there were many of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. What clothes did the gentlemen wear?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Blue camouflage, green camouflage, dark green.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Was anybody in civilian clothes or only people in camouflage at your courtyard?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: There was nobody in civilian clothes. All of them were dressed in camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And what language did the gentlemen speak?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you describe what they wore on their faces, if anything.

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Some of them had masks; their faces were covered. Some of them had their faces painted, and some, normal.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And what weapons, if any, did the gentlemen wear?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Automatic rifles, machine-guns, and I don't know all the names of these weapons. Whatever type of weapon there was and existed, they had it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And how did the gentlemen arrive to your courtyard?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: On tanks, Pinzgauer, and there was also on foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you describe the colour of the tanks or the Pinzgauers.

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: There were green and blue, the two types.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Plain or camouflage?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: That I don't remember. I was horrified.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Any markings, symbols, on the tanks or Pinzgauers?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Some of them, the people, they had the red ribbons tied on their arms. This is what we noticed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I was asking whether any symbols were marked on the vehicles with which the gentlemen arrived.

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: The Serbian symbol.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And what did the Serbian symbol say? If you don't remember --

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Their flag was on them, the flag of the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So what happened when the gentlemen arrived?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: My son, Blerim Malaj, at the time of their arrival was in the toilet outside. They spotted him the first, immediately, and made him lie on the ground. They were shouting and yelling. My husband went out, and they told my husband to call on us, all of us, and tell us to come outside, so this is what he did. He called on us; we came all outside. And when I was in the courtyard I saw my son lying on the ground, my son Blerim.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If I can just stop you here. How old was your son Blerim that morning?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Fifteen and a half.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: I started to scream because they had made him lie down, and a soldier or a policeman - I cannot describe him - he was holding him at gunpoint, and he ordered my son to turn his head on the other side so that he could not see me. This is what my son did. Then they stopped my husband, my nephew, my brother --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I just stop you for a second, please. You said a gentleman held your son at gunpoint. What did he have in his hands, this gentleman?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: He had an automatic rifle, a weapon with a long barrel, and he was holding that on my son's head.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So he was very close to your son, in fact.

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Yes, yes. On his head, very close to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What did the gentleman with the automatic rifle wear?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Blue camouflage.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Then you mentioned already your husband. Can you please continue? I had interrupted you.

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: My husband Vat Malaj was also forced to lie on the ground. There were three vehicles nearby; one car belongs to us and two to my brothers. They asked for the keys, the car keys. We didn't have them. My brother's cars, my husband and Arben Kabashi were forced to show them how they can use the wires to start the car, and after that they were again ordered to lay on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Meaning Vat Malaj and Arben Kabashi also were lying on the ground, having been to the cars in the meantime?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What happened in relation to the house of your brother Nikoll Kabashi?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: A policeman with a blue camouflage uniform went to that house, opened the door -- broke down the door and forced Nikoll and all his family out, asked for their personal documents. Nikoll and Andrush provided him with the -- their IDs, while Nikoll's wife, his daughters and son, they were all ordered to go outside, while Nikoll and Andrush were forced to lie on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Who was Andrush Kabashi?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: My nephew, my brother's son, Nikoll Kabashi's son.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: How old was he in 1999?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Eighteen, Andrush.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So overall your family and Nikoll Kabashi's family were in the courtyard. How many people were there, meaning Albanian -- Kosovo Albanian people?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Seventeen.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I note the time. Maybe this is a good point for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We will have a break now and resume in half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm reminded, Mr. Neuner, before we break that there hasn't been an exhibit made of the map that was marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Correct. Your Honours, I was intending to ask the witness at some later point in time to mark one additional circle on it. That's why I didn't ask for it to be tendered now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The problem is that we are likely, then, to lose all the present markings because of time delay.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Then I would ask that it be tendered now, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00294, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We'll have the break now and resume in half an hour, at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Before the break you told us that there were 17 Kosovo Albanians in your courtyard on the 27th of April, in the morning. Could you tell me, had any of these 17 persons any weapons?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: No, none of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Were the 35 men who were coming to your courtyard searching for weapons?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: No, they didn't search for weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So what happened after Nikoll and Andrush and Arben Kabashi and your husband, Vat, and your son Blerim were told to lay down? What happened next?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: We were ordered to leave the house and walk ourselves to Albania.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Who are you referring to by "we"?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: My family, the 17 of us, brothers, nephews. Nikoll's family and my husband's family, Arben's family.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Who, if anybody, stayed behind in the compound of your family, in the courtyard?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Only the five of them; my husband Vat, Blerim, Nikoll, Andrush and Arben, because they were held there, nobody else. And immediately after that I heard the gun-shots and I heard screams, which was a scream that was horrible, and it was my son's voice that I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you mention the name of your -- the given name of your son?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Blerim Malaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And how far were you away when you heard the gun-shots and your son Blerim?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: About 50 metres away. I tried to go back but one of them did not let me return.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Who did not let you return?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: A policeman who was sitting on a tank.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And why do you believe he was a policeman?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: He was. He was wearing blue clothes. How do I know? He said, It's better for you to continue on your way. He pointed the gun at me, on my chest.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you just, coming back to the clothes he wore, clarify. Were they civilian clothes he was wearing?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: No. It was a uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And what exactly did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: I tried to go back to the courtyard to see my son, my husband, and he said, You'd better go with your children than go back and be executed or killed. One of the children who was with me, Bekim, he is here, he took my hand and said, Please, mom, don't leave us alone. Come with us. And because of the children I decided to go back.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And did the policeman tell you where to go? Where to?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: He ordered me to go to Albania and not to go home.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What did you observe about your houses when you were trying to look back?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: The houses were on fire. I could see the smoke. And the ones that were lying on the ground, they had been executed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: But you didn't see that they had been executed.

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: No, not at that moment when I was present. But when I turned my back, immediately after that it happened, and I heard my son's voice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I was asking about the houses, and you said they were in flames. Could you tell me which houses you saw in flames?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: My houses and all the houses in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: On your compound there was also, you had told us, the house of your brother Nikoll. What did you observe about that house?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: It was on fire as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And where did you go?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: We took the main road, Korenice-Gjakove.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I ask you what you observed within the village, first of all? You mentioned there were some houses in flames. What exactly did you observe?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: We could see the houses set on fire. Families -- other families from the villages, the Binakus, the Kamberis, from my neighbourhood, had left their homes. They were all leaving. Women and children were on the road, and the men had been held in their courtyards. That's what they said, and that's what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: How many houses did you see burning, roughly, that day?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: As far as I could see, they started with our family first, the Malaj family, but the total number of houses was about 10 or 15 at the same time that were set on fire. All of them were on fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And you said you took the main road, Korenice-Gjakove.

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Who, if anybody, was escorting you?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: The army, the police, they were lining the road, and they were forcing us to walk on and not stop anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. How many persons were in your group?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: A lot of us. Quite a few. I can't give you an exact number. But we were among the first.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can we, with the usher's assistance, pull up the map which was shown earlier, P294, which has been admitted as P294.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Were there people only coming from Korenica who joined the group, or were there people also coming from other villages that day?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: That day there were people from other villages as well, such as Guska. There were people who were staying there in Guska. The whole village of Guska had left, but also other -- people from other villages were leaving, such as Junik, people from Gjakove, Skivjane, and they were on the road to Prizren.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you, first of all, mark the direction of your movement on this map. Where did you go to?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Yes. We went towards Albania, Korenice-Gjakove, Gjakove-Prizren, Prizren-Verbica, and then to the border with Albania.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I think that's enough. You went towards Gjakove, yeah?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And can you explain the direction by drawing some arrows the way the villagers were coming.

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Yes. People were from Guska. Guska is here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you next to the cross you marked there, mark the number 7, please, where you believe Guska is.

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Yes, I will write the number here. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Maybe just if you could -- we see here on the map Korenica. If you start to draw an arrow to the right of Korenica, to the right of the number 6, what you had marked as Suhadoll earlier, towards Djakovica, an arrow to indicate your movement, first of all.

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes. And can you now mark from where the villagers came who joined your convoy.

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: From Skivjane -- would you like me to circle it?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: So Skivjane.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you mark the direction of movement from Skivjan.

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes. Next to Skivjan could you please mark an 8.

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Which other places?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: From Gjakove.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You yourself went to Djakovica. You just encircled it. Please mark a 9 next to your circle.

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You mentioned to us you went to Djakovica. Could you tell us, were there any check-points along the road from Korenica towards Djakovica?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Yes. Towards the Tabaku bridge, Ura e Tabakeve.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you mark or encircle the location of the check-point and mark a 10 next to it, please.

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And who was manning that check-point on that day?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: The forces, the Serb forces, police, soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And having been at the check-point, where -- in which direction did you proceed?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: As soon as we got there, we were not allowed to go anywhere else, so we continued straight to Prizren.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you mark on this map where Prizren -- which direction Prizren is, only by drawing an arrow pointing towards Prizren indicating your movement. Prizren is not on this map, just that you show us which direction you were moving.

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you make this an arrow, please.

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. And from Djakovica which direction did you move, north, south, east, west?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: East.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. Can you just mark with an arrow east of Djakovica in which direction you were moving.

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you mark an arrow east of Djakovica? I mean you're always marking the city centre of Djakovica here, but could you mark east of Djakovica to indicate the direction of movement, behind Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have to intervene.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that the Prosecutor does not have the right to lead the witness, telling her where to put the arrow. She must put the arrow where she thinks it should be, to the best of her knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, I saw no sign of the Prosecution leading the witness. He was trying to get a more clear indication drawn by the witness of the direction of a major geographic centre, so that I don't think there is an issue there. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree with this, Your Honour, but I don't think that he should say, Draw the arrow to the east. He should say, Draw the arrow where you actually went. But I do agree that this must be clarified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Carry on, please, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I ask that this map be tendered, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: With the further markings, it will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00295, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What I would like to learn is, when you left Korenica on the 27th of April, 1999, to proceed on this way you have just drawn for us, did you leave voluntarily?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: No. We were forced.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: On that day, the 27th of April, 1999, were there any NATO air-strikes which targeted Korenica?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Any air-strikes from NATO which targeted the wider region west of Djakovica?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: No, not that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So what was the real reason that you left Korenica that day?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: The truth is that we were forced out. Our husbands and sons were held, nephews as well, and we were told to leave. We were not allowed to stay. And they were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to have 65 ter number 615, and there page 22, being shown now. And this is a map, again. I just need one image on the screen. Yes. Maybe we can focus on the area between Djakovica and Prizren, because the witness has shown us -- yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you now mark the area or the streets -- the direction of your movement from Djakovica, please.

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Can you zoom in, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can we zoom in a little bit further. I think Djakovica can go on the upper part of this image. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I hope that's sufficient.

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: It must not be a hundred percent precise. The important point is that you indicate being at Djakovica, where you went. What was the next major town to which you went?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: This road.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If you could just mark along the road with your pencil to where you went.

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Just by drawing a straight line, this would be the best.

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: A full line, not interrupted?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: A full line is maybe the easiest. Correct.

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And to which major town did you finally come to?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Can we erase this? Yeah, in the direction of Prizren. I made a mistake. Sorry, I didn't see Prizren here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Is that possible? The witness has drawn -- can we erase that? I think she's -- okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We'll start afresh. So if you could, afresh, just mark by drawing a straight line.

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. Can you, by marking an arrow, just indicating -- indicate the direction of movement.

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: You mean from Prizren onwards?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: No, from Djakovica onwards. Which direction did you move?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: So from Gjakove, all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could I ask that this map is tendered, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00296, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We have a further map, but it doesn't show Prizren on it, so I would just ask a few questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: From Prizren, where did you proceed to?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Towards the border.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: With?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: At Morina.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: To which --

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Prizren, Verbica and Cafe Morina.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And the border is between Kosovo where you were and which state, please?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: And Kosova, former Yugoslavia at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes. You were in Kosovo, obviously, but the border faces which other country, please?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Albania.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. Throughout all your way from Korenica towards the border to Kosovo -- border to Albania, did you have any possibility of changing your directions?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: No, we didn't have this possibility. They didn't allow us.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Who is "they" who did not allow you?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: The forces, the Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And could you be a little bit more precise, which type of forces, Serb forces, you're talking about?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Police, paramilitary. We were escorted by them up to the border, and they didn't give us even five minutes for rest or to have something to eat or drink. They didn't allow us to sit anywhere for a rest.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Did you make any attempt to change your direction?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: That was impossible.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: But my question was: Did you yourself or your group try to change the direction, to go somewhere else than to Prizren and the border to Albania?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Yes. When we were at Gjakove, at the part near the hospital, we attempted to leave. We called the priest. We call him Father Marijan. I don't know his last name. We thought that we would go to Rac or Mulic, but the police didn't let us. They just said, You either go straight to Albania, or we will execute you. So we were given these two choices: Either to go to Albania or remain there and be executed. So they didn't let us go to any other direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And what happened -- what, if anything, happened at the border to the ID documents, the identification documents, passports, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: They asked for the identification documents. Those who had them on them, they did give them. I didn't have one. Those who had tractors were forced to remove the registration plates from their tractors.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you tell me, who is "they" who asked for the documents and registration plates?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: The police, those that serve at the border.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And are we talking about the police being on the Kosovar side of the border or about the police being on the Albanian side of the border?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: The policemen on the Kosovar side of the border.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: At what time did you receive leave Korenica on the 27th of April, 1999?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: At 7.30. At 8.00 we were already on the main road, and we left our house at 7.30 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And at what time did you reach Vrbica or the border near Vrbica or Cafe Morina, the border to Albania?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: On the 28th of April, at 1.00 p.m. Around 12.00 or 1.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So you went to Albania. When did you return to Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: On the 3rd of July, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: How did the houses in your courtyard in Korenica look like?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: They were burnt down, destroyed, and one could no longer live in them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You had mentioned that on the 27th of April, 1999, there were three vehicles belonging to the families in the courtyard, in the courtyard in Korenica. I'm referring to the vehicles of your brother and of your own family. What happened to these vehicles -- what did you see or observe about these vehicles?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: These cars were burnt down. One of them, which was just in front of my gate, it was an Audi make, they tried to take it with them but they couldn't, and they set it on fire. And the other two cars, one belonging to my husband and one to my brother, they were both Mercedes make, they were burnt inside the courtyard. And there was a tree also in the courtyard, and it was burnt down, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What was the condition of the house of your brother Nikoll?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Burnt down.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Was it inhabitable when you saw it again?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: No, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: When and what did you learn about the fate of your five relatives that you had left and last seen in your courtyard on the 27th of April, 1999? If you could please start with your husband, Vat Malaj.

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: According to ICRC and the examinations, we were informed that his body was found at Batanice. His funeral took place on the 17th of April, 2004. This was very hard news for me. My son, Blerim Malaj, I was informed of him a year later, on the 27th of April, 2005, when he was reburied. His body was recovered at Batanice. My brother Nikoll Kabashi, his -- we collected his body together with my son's body on the same day, on the 27th of April. My nephew Arben Kabashi, Sokol Kabashi's son - Sokol Kabashi is my eldest brother - on the 14th of December, 2005, was reburied. That's when we got his body. Andrush Kabashi, too, was reburied on the 27th of April. We received all these bodies from Batanice. I saw all of them, identified them, and we reburied them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Where did you see these bodies?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: We collected the bodies in Rahovec. That's where the location was, where these bodies were brought to. This is where we first saw him, in Rahovec, and we took them from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And do you know who transported the bodies to Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: The International Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. Could you just tell in which year you were informed about your brother Nikoll Kabashi? You mentioned the date, 27 of April, but not the year.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned that all bodies were found in Batajnica. In what state lies Batajnica?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: In Serbia, near Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: For Your Honours' reference, all the names of the victims just mentioned by our witness, these names are mentioned in Schedule H of our indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What I wanted to ask you, Ms. Malaj, is you mentioned a couple of other families in relation to Korenica; for example, the Dedaj family. What, if anything, has happened to the Dedaj family on the 27th of April, 1999?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: The Dedaj family, on this day, took refuge to the mountains. My younger brother Jakob Kabashi, my mother, Marika Kabashi, they stayed there, too. They went to the mountains. The first attack was on my family because my house is just before the Dedaj family houses. They survived, the whole family. My mother, my younger brother, they all survived because they fled to the mountains.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you know a person by the name of Merita Dedaj?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you know the name of her father?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: Mark.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What happened to Mark Dedaj?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: He was also killed in Korenice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: On the 27th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Which year?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And can you tell us, how did you learn about this fact?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: The remains of these victims all came from Batanice. She reburied her father's remains, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And where did she bury her father's remains, if you know?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: In Guska.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And where are the five relatives or family members of your family buried nowadays?

utterances.speaker: LIZANE MALAJ
utterances.text: In Meje.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you for answering all my questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no further questions at this point in time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Neuner. It is now the time we must finish for the day to allow another trial to continue, so we will adjourn now. We continue tomorrow in the afternoon at 2.15, and I expect it will be in Courtroom I. So if you can understand, we must now adjourn because another trial continues here, but we will continue your evidence tomorrow in the afternoon. People will look after you until then. Thank you. We now adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 11th day of February, 2009, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.47 p.m.,
